summary:
My project is an immersive, illustrated storytelling experience developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge that catalogs discarded lunar and Martian artifacts.
 Blending my deep passion for space sciences with my love for visual storytelling, I developed a narrative-driven catalog that breathes life into off-world historical markers, with a special focus on my biggest muse: the Ingenuity Mars helicopter.
It addresses the challenge by transforming cold, forgotten scientific debris into emotional narratives. Rather than just presenting data, I use my original drawings and illustrations to map the artifacts' resting locations and document their final moments.

 This artistic approach makes the reality of space missions more accessible, connecting audiences to the hardware we leave behind through a deeply personal, visual lens.
This work is important because it preserves our off-world heritage and educates the public about humanity's permanent footprint in the cosmos. By illustrating Ingenuity’s journey and final resting place on the red dust, the project honors the resilience of human ambition. It ensures that even after these incredible machines stop operating, their pioneering legacy and the spirit of exploration are never forgotten.
details:
Project Overview and Functionality The project is an immersive, illustrated storytelling catalog that maps and documents discarded lunar and Martian artifacts. Rather than presenting a dry database of space debris, it visually chronicles the resting places and final moments of these historical markers, with a central focus on the Ingenuity Mars helicopter. It works by guiding the audience through narrative logs that breathe life into the cold hardware left behind on alien surfaces, transforming mechanical end-of-life data into a tribute to exploration.

Benefits and Intended Impact By turning scientific hardware into emotional narratives, the project makes the realities of space exploration deeply accessible to the general public. The intended impact is to preserve humanity's off-world heritage and highlight our permanent footprint in the cosmos. It ensures that the pioneering legacy of machines like Ingenuity—which defied the odds on the red dust—is honored and remembered. Ultimately, the project aims to bridge visual arts and planetary sciences, ensuring that these monuments of human ambition are never forgotten.

Tools and Software The visual mapping and emotional core of the project rely on digital illustration. All original artwork, bringing the Martian and lunar artifacts to life, was drawn entirely using Ibis Paint or images taken from Pinterest. This software was used to reconstruct these off-world monuments visually, blending creative digital design with research into the artifacts' histories and resting environments.

Creativity and Team Factors The true creativity of this project lies in its profound resilience, mirroring the very themes of Martian exploration it seeks to honor. Operating as a one-person team, the development process hit a critical failure point when almost all the project data was lost during the original creation phase. Instead of abandoning the mission, the primary factor considered was how to push forward. Tapping into the same spirit as the Perseverance rover, the project was completely rebuilt from the ground up. This solo undertaking required immense dedication, and that struggle directly informed the final artwork—infusing the illustrations with a genuine sense of survival, endurance, and deep love for space
